win_claim.quote: Experimental results on diverse set of benchmark datasets with and without noise proved that our RBO algorithm could be an useful alternative for SMOTE-based solutions, especially when dealing with complex data distributions.

notes: No per-dataset results in the paper: all results tables (2-10) are average rankings over 24 KEEL datasets (final analysis, Table 1 bottom; 10 others used only for preliminary parameter study). Complete per-dataset results stated to be at https://github.com/michalkoziarski/RBO (not read). Table 2 page rendered and checked visually; text extraction matched. In Table 2 CART G-mean, best (lowest) rank printed bold is ADASYN 2.9167 with '-' subscript (significantly better than RBO); SMOTE G-mean rank for CART has no significance mark. G-mean ranks for other classifiers (Table 2): k-NN RBO 4.9167 / SMOTE 2.5000(-, bold); SVM RBO 4.0833 / SMOTE 3.7500 (ADASYN 2.6667 bold); NB RBO 3.0000 (bold) / SMOTE 4.3750. Table 3 level 0.00 row repeats Table 2 CART values. Other conditions: label noise {0.05,0.1,0.15,0.20} (Tables 3-6), feature noise {0.1..0.5} (Tables 7-10). Text extraction rendered zeros as '4.0 0 0 0' etc.; normalized to printed '4.0000'.
